blocks.orig: Tanzania is a popular destination for avid hikers who seek unmatched views and unspoilt landscapes, inhabited by indigenous tribes and wild animals. Here, you’ll witness the limitless beauty of Mother Nature and conquer mountains, from which peaks you can take in the most breathtaking views. Find out, which five Tanzania hikes are so stunning that they’re worth sore legs.
blocks.html: Keen hikers come to Tanzania for views you won’t find elsewhere and untouched landscapes, home to indigenous tribes and wildlife. This is where you can take in the boundless beauty of nature and climb mountains whose summits reward you with remarkable panoramas. Read on to see which five hikes in Tanzania are beautiful enough to justify aching legs.

blocks.orig: When thinking of hiking in Tanzania, Mount Kilimanjaro comes to mind instantly – it is Africa’s highest mountain, after all. As alluring as it might sound, this hike is not for the light-hearted and requires a lot of preparation. There are several trails leading to the top, with the climb itself taking at least five days. However, it’s very important to take into account your physical skills and trekking experience when choosing your ideal route. Also, adding one or two days to your hiking adventure will increase the chances of you standing on the Roof of Africa.
blocks.html: Mention hiking in Tanzania and most people immediately think of Mount Kilimanjaro – Africa’s highest mountain, after all. However tempting it sounds, this climb is not one for the faint-hearted, and it takes serious preparation. Several trails lead to the summit, and the ascent alone lasts at least five days. That is why it matters to weigh up your fitness and trekking experience when you pick the route that suits you. Adding an extra day or two to the trek will also improve your odds of reaching the Roof of Africa.

blocks.orig: Hike on Mount Meru to the First Camp (Miriakamba)
blocks.html: Day hike on Mount Meru to the first camp (Miriakamba)

blocks.orig: If Mount Kilimanjaro is on your bucket list, but you want to start small, how about conquering a part of Mount Meru? On your way to the Miriakamba Huts, you’ll cross rainforests and get a chance to spot wild animals like zebras, monkeys, antelopes, elephants, and giraffes – so be sure to have your camera close.
blocks.html: Is Mount Kilimanjaro on your wish list, but would you rather begin with something smaller? Then why not take on a section of Mount Meru? The trail to the Miriakamba Huts leads you through rainforest, with a good chance of seeing wildlife such as zebras, monkeys, antelopes, elephants and giraffes – so keep your camera within reach.

blocks.orig: Ngorongoro Crater appeared too crowded for your taste? Then go and explore a still outstanding but less busy option! We’re talking about the Empakaai Crater. But be aware: the view of the lake from the crater edge will take your breath away! Only for a little while, though. It will come back just in time to hike down to the lake, where you’ll be greeted by countless colourful flamingos. If the weather allows, you’ll even see Lake Natron and Ol Doinyo Lengai, the mountain of the Maasai gods.
blocks.html: Did Ngorongoro Crater feel too busy for you? Then head to an alternative that is just as impressive yet far quieter: the Empakaai Crater. A word of warning, though: looking down at the lake from the crater rim will leave you breathless! Not for long, mind you. You’ll have your breath back in time for the walk down to the lake, where countless colourful flamingos await. On a clear day you can even make out Lake Natron and Ol Doinyo Lengai, the mountain of the Maasai gods.

blocks.orig: Climb the Mountain of God: Ol Doinyo Lengai
blocks.html: Climbing the Mountain of God: Ol Doinyo Lengai

blocks.orig: Ol Doinyo Lengai is a must-visit active volcano that offers one of the most fascinating Tanzania hikes ever. Not only does it have the coolest lava on Earth, but it also boasts a unique composition of lava that resembles black oil. In fact, Ol Doinyo Lengai is the only volcano to have natrocarbonatite lava that turns white as soon as it comes into contact with water.
blocks.html: An active volcano you really should visit, Ol Doinyo Lengai offers one of the most fascinating hikes in Tanzania. It has the coolest lava on Earth, and on top of that a unique lava composition that looks like black oil. Ol Doinyo Lengai is in fact the only volcano with natrocarbonatite lava, which turns white the moment it touches water.

blocks.orig: As you ascend the mountain, you will get the point why the local tribe called it the Mountain of Gods – especially when you step onto the volcanic ash and witness the spectacular views from above. Make sure to wear slip-resistant shoes, since the descent is just as challenging as the ascent.
blocks.html: Climbing higher, you will understand why the local tribe named it the Mountain of Gods – above all once you walk on the volcanic ash and see the spectacular views below you. Wear shoes with a good grip, because coming down is every bit as demanding as going up.

blocks.orig: Walking Safari inside Arusha National Park
blocks.html: A walking safari in Arusha National Park

blocks.orig: A half-day hike through the scenic Arusha National Park is perfect to rewind and reconnect with nature. Meeting wild safari animals eye-to-eye is the ultimate Tanzania hiking experience if you prefer not put in too much physical effort. Here, you’ll get a chance to take close-up photos of giraffes, zebras, warthogs, and other local wildlife whilst admiring Lake Momella, taking a dip in the waterfall, and even seeing the Ngurdoto Crater from afar.
blocks.html: Spending half a day on foot in the scenic Arusha National Park is an ideal way to unwind and reconnect with nature. If you would rather not exert yourself too much, coming face to face with wild safari animals is the ultimate hiking experience in Tanzania. You can take close-up photos of giraffes, zebras, warthogs and other local wildlife, admire Lake Momella, take a dip in the waterfall and even catch a distant view of the Ngurdoto Crater.

blocks.orig: If you cannot wait to lace up your hiking boots now, consider planning your journey when the weather is not boiling hot. That way, you can hike for longer hours and have a cool breeze cool you down on the way. June to October or January to February are ideal for a trekking tour around Tanzania since the weather is drier. Also, the off-season from January to February, would allow you to enjoy the landscape without the noise of the crowd.
blocks.html: Can’t wait to put on your hiking boots? Then plan your trip for a time when it isn’t scorching hot. You’ll be able to walk for longer, with a cool breeze to refresh you along the way. Because the weather is drier, June to October or January to February are ideal months for trekking in Tanzania. The off-season from January to February also lets you take in the scenery without the bustle of crowds.
